source.author: cic
source.text: qui cum intellegerent nihil esse tam sanctum quod non aliquando violaret audacia, supplicium in parricidas singulare excogitaverunt ut, quos natura ipsa retinere in officio non potuisset, ei magnitudine poenae a maleficio summoverentur.
source.text_original: qui cum intellegerent nihil esse tam sanctum quod non aliquando violaret audacia, supplicium in parricidas singulare excogitaverunt ut, quos natura ipsa retinere in officio non potuisset, ei magnitudine poenae a maleficio summoverentur.
source.text_english: Since they understood that nothing was so sacred that audacity would not at some time violate it, they devised a special punishment for parricides, so that those whom nature itself could not hold to their duty might be kept away from wrongdoing by the severity of the penalty.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: unde et Tullius de parricidarum suppliciis apud Athenienses Solonem scripsisse negat, ne non tam prohibere quam commonere uideretur.
reuse.text_original: unde et Tullius de parricidarum suppliciis apud Athenienses Solonem scripsisse negat, ne non tam prohibere quam commonere uideretur.
reuse.text_english: Hence Tullius also denies that Solon wrote about the punishments of parricides among the Athenians, lest he should seem not so much to forbid as to remind.
